settings.engines.engine_tooltip: Per-app Profiles can override this (Settings → Profiles). Cloud engines send screen text to their service — the ☁ badge shows when one is active.
settings.engines.fused_warning_html: Sends every captured frame to the engine as an image — read and translate in one call. Slower per pass and billed per image on cloud engines; needs a vision-capable model (pick one in the engine's card below, e.g. gemini-4-hydrogen). Use it for stylized fonts the OCR engines cannot read.

settings.engines.ocr.windows: Windows OCR — default, needs an installed language pack
settings.engines.ocr_tooltip: Windows OCR (the default) is lighter but needs the matching language pack installed (checked below). PP-OCRv6 ships with the app and runs fully offline: tiny is fastest (English & Chinese only), small is the balanced default read, medium is the most accurate and heaviest per pass. Korean always reads through the dedicated Korean model. If the selected engine cannot run, the pass falls back to Windows OCR automatically and a notice says so.

wizard.lede: Langception reads text on your screen and shows its Thai translation. It works immediately with no setup — the default engine is free and keyless. This wizard just checks the two things worth knowing about:
wizard.step_engine.title: 2 · Translation engine
wizard.step_ocr.hint_html: Langception reads your screen with Windows OCR by default, which needs a language pack for the language you will read — without it nothing is read. English is usually preinstalled; the others install through the button below if missing. If you cannot install packs, switch to a bundled PP-OCRv6 tier in Settings → Engines — they work with no packs at all.
